Sara — thanks, clear ask. Outlining what we'll deliver and how we'll hook it into your staging pipeline so procurement has what they need. TL;DR: we can deliver a CSV prompt set + eval harness integration (webhook + Slack) and a conservative canary policy that auto-rolls back only on severe regressions; non-severe failures create immediate regression alerts and block promotion until triaged.

Deliverables (we'll attach samples):
- Prompt set: CSV with columns: id, prompt, context_tags, expected_labels, tolerance_notes. We'll send a v1 CSV by EOD 10/11.
- Eval harness integration: Redwood will run nightly evals against your staging model. Results will be pushed to a secure S3/Drive link and a summary posted to a dedicated Slack channel; critical failures will fire a Pager-like webhook you can subscribe to.
- Regression alerts: three levels: INFO (metric drift), WARN (threshold exceeded on non-critical tests), CRITICAL (SLO breach or hallucination spike). CRITICAL -> automatic canary rollback; WARN -> block promotion + paged to CS/engineer; INFO -> digest.
- Canary & rollback policy: initial canary rollout at 5% traffic in staging (mirrors production routing); rollback trigger = CRITICAL signal from eval harness OR sustained >3% increase in hallucination rate over baseline for 3 consecutive runs. Manual rollback flow: CS + eng on-call required.

Proposed owners & dates:
- 10/11 (today): Redwood sends prompt_set_v1.csv and eval_integration_notes.pdf (Grace)
- 10/12–10/16: Nebula team validates prompt set and flags missing cases (Sara)
- 10/18: Staging evals begin with nightly runs (Redwood ops + Nebula staging)
- 10/24: Final signoff decision point (Procurement + Sara)

Open questions for you:
1) Do you want eval results forwarded into your issue tracker (we can post to Jira) or only Slack?
2) Who on your side should be the emergency contact for a CRITICAL rollback (name + mobile)?

Attachments: qmon_prompt_set_v1.csv (sample), eval_harness_integration_notes.pdf (integration hooks + webhook schema)

I'll loop Karthik for the rollout policy details.

Best,
Grace O'Connor

Sara / team — quick technical clarifications from the implementation side so your engineers can scope the staging work: 

- Prompt set format: recommend CSV for initial handoff (we supplied sample). Each row maps to an eval case; expected_labels can be single label or JSON-encoded list (we include examples in the sample CSV).
- Eval harness hooking: we provide a lightweight client that posts predictions to the harness endpoint; if you prefer, we can run the harness in your VPC via a small container we provide. Either way, the output is a JSON results file per run (summary + per-case rows).
- Alerting cadence: default is immediate CRITICAL alerts (webhook + Slack) and a daily digest for INFO/WARN; we can shorten cadence on request.
- Canary guardrails: to reduce noise early, the canary will require 2 consecutive CRITICAL runs (separated by at least 1 hour) OR a single CRITICAL with >5% absolute regression to trigger auto-rollback. That reduces flapping for noisy cases.

Implementation checklist for your engineers:
1) Add our harness client to staging network allowlist (we'll share IP ranges).
2) Confirm S3 bucket or Drive location and give Redwood write permissions.
3) Provide webhook endpoint for CRITICAL alerts (we can fallback to email if needed).
4) Share primary on-call contact for 24–48 hour window during canary.

I'll open a Jira ticket and attach integration examples to speed the work — referencing D-5579. If you want us to run the first night of evals with you on a call, we can schedule a 1-hr debug slot on 10/18.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
